review_author.identity: Codex resource-resume worker, reviewing Pascal-authored all16 bridge
review_author.disclosure: Authored escrow/resource_resume Rust dependencies, resource tests, earlier seven-rule parity sidecar, and v2 recognizer/vector work. Previously provided Pascal with resource API and bounded bootstrap-port scope advice. Did not author or edit the reviewed all16 Rust test or Lean oracle. This is a same-model review with partial authorship/dependency independence, not a clean-context cross-model or human audit.

scope: Typed input projection and absence of Rust expected-output feedback into Lean
Every native rule represented; full Snapshot and native-expression fullFold observations
Actual Rust binary snapshot encode/decode continuation at every cut
Finite input-derived value/key/signer/address universes for the actual corpus
Negative controls must compile, execute, emit JSON, and then diverge semantically
Explicit unproved bounded protocol and resource classification ports

checks.expected_output_separation: Rust expected values are produced by Summary.render and checked against native state::fold. They remain in Rust. Generated Lean input consists only of authenticated Act projections, address ranks, recognized HLC pairs, cause metadata, cast bindings, initial allocations and headroom; no Rust Outcome/Value or expected array enters Event, ports, resourceData or classify.
checks.native_ids_and_order: SignedMessage::sign then authenticate produces actual Acts. BTreeSet of complete state-wire hashes and references assigns ascending Nat ranks. Signer ranks use ascending ASCII signer names in this corpus, preserving Rust UTF-8 byte order. Event address keys are converted to the same ranks for comparison only.
checks.all_rules: Rust clause and Lean raw/resolveFields include all sixteen heads. Lean fields.length=16 is kernel-checked with decide. Numeric SetUnion is nonempty in the two data-bearing cases: native SetUnion selects distinct complete field values, not list elements.
checks.snapshot_cuts: Rust reconstructs each prefix only to create a checkpoint, then calls Summary::decode_for(saved.encode(), clause, protocol). The decoded object is the one advanced through the tail; it is not replaced by a fresh prefix fold. Lean observations independently call Snapshot.checkpoint on take(cut), then advance on the bounded dropped tail. Every cut and every following prefix is enumerated.
checks.baseline: Both Lean Snapshot.render and CheckpointAll.fullFold are compared to Rust at each prefix/cut. Rust Summary.render is separately compared to state::fold after each delivery. Lean fullFold is the native-expression evaluator over normalized accepted identities. Protocol/resource port implementations are shared by the two Lean paths, so they are not independent general native-classifier proofs.
checks.finite_universe: For this corpus all selected v values are integers, application keys are x/y strings, event keys are ranked input addresses, signer keys are ASCII names, and title is a direct scalar cell. Values come from all input v fields; keys include all input k fields, signer values and event addresses; histogram supports come from input values. These domains cover every support value attainable by the declared rules on this corpus. Title is rendered directly. No expected outputs determine a query universe.
checks.progress_port: The generated cause maps a recognized tick parent of verb open to begin and retains subsequent tick parent IDs. Bound=3 and thread rank=0 are fixed for the one-thread, one-repeat-chain fixture. No position number computed by Rust is supplied to Lean.
checks.resource_port: Rust project_resource_fact/allocations supply input facts, not native verifier outcomes. Lean independently recognizes the exact fixture cast and allocations/headroom and classifies a bootstrap-only account state. Literal ready rights/headroom are justified only by that exact recognized input subset; this is not a generic escrow algorithm. Empty/pre-opener states classify pending. All corpus cases deliver one valid root before one linked opener; later events contain no native resource operation.
checks.negative_controls: run_lean asserts successful Lean compilation/execution and parses JSON before any control comparison. Controls change a selected numeric projection (r11), a repeat causal parent (r14), or an input initial allocation (r15). The driver requires equal record counts and at least one target-field mismatch. A compile failure cannot count as a rejected control. The altered resource allocation leaves the recognized bootstrap subset; its divergent result is not claimed to reproduce the native fault outside that subset.
checks.trust_boundary: No extraction proof, native codec proof, native admission proof, signature proof, general escrow classifier proof, arbitrary protocol-port correctness or new resource authority follows from this finite run. Existing formal proof trust/axiom audits are separate from this review.

constraints: Three deterministic cases; selected integers and ASCII strings only. No claim for arbitrary lists, Unicode escaping, missing selected fields or unrecognized clocks.
The bridge authenticates signed messages but treats the fixture as admitted; ordinary installation/shape/role/admission evidence belongs to separate lifecycle tests.
Progress port is a recognized single-verb chain with the known opener edge mapped to begin; arbitrary fan-in, missing/late tick predecessors, cycles and cross-thread evidence are not covered.

Resource port covers only fixed floor0/ceiling20 bootstrap allocations10/0 and headroom5/5 under the exact fixture cast. No resource ledger operations, forks, wrong dependencies, malformed facts, Collective or Quorum outcomes are exercised by this bridge.
Resource input contract is an identity-consistent accepted store. Raw conflicting signed attempts and native AST-alias attempt lists are separate diagnostic/evidence concerns.
Initial witness order, serialized Rust/Lean byte equality, and general source extraction are not compared.
7392 counts two field comparisons per rule-prefix-cut (Snapshot and fullFold), not 7392 independent histories or proof obligations.

retracted_concerns.initial_concern: Reviewer initially assumed SetUnion flattened list elements and numeric v would never update it.
retracted_concerns.resolution: False positive: native state.rs1016 uses distinct(acts,field), Rust summary inserts whole canonical field values, and Lean CheckpointData.SetUnion inserts the same values. Concern retracted immediately to Pascal and main. Author added an explicit nonempty-union-prefix assertion; observed counts are10 and11 in the two data-bearing cases. No flattening or unsupported semantic change requested.

next_action: Main can consume this bounded review with its partial-independence disclosure. No implementation correction remains requested by this review.
